career_ladder.note: Senior Section Engineers (SSE) head operational divisions and technical sections across Civil (P-Way, Works, Bridges), Mechanical (Workshops, Loco, Carriage & Wagon), Electrical (Traction, General Services), and Signal & Telecommunication cadres of Indian Railways. SSEs represent the pinnacle of the Group 'C' technical hierarchy and serve as the primary feeder cadre for induction into the Indian Railway Service of Engineers (IRSE) and Group 'B' Gazetted management ranks.

exam_scheme.note: Recruitment for Senior Section Engineer is governed by Railway Board technical recruitment regulations (RBE No. 59/2021). Selection is conducted through a single or two-stage Computer Based Test (CBT) covering Discipline-Specific Engineering domains (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics & Telecommunication) alongside General Aptitude. The examination comprises 150 questions for 150 marks over 120 minutes with 1/3 (0.33) marks negative penalty, followed by Document Verification and Medical Examination.

financial_package.pay_source_label: 7th CPC Pay Matrix, Railway Civilian Employees, Government of India
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated at Level 7 entry basic pay (₹44,900) with 58% DA (₹26,042), HRA (9%/18%/27% as per city tier: ₹4,041 to ₹12,123), and Transport Allowance (₹3,600 + DA = ₹5,688 in higher TPTA cities). Senior Section Engineers in open-line and breakdown depots also receive Site Inspection Allowance and Breakdown Allowance.
official_perks: All-India free 1st Class / 2nd AC Railway Passes and Privilege Ticket Orders (PTOs) for self and family
Free comprehensive medical healthcare in Indian Railway Hospitals and referral super-specialty hospitals
Allotment of Type-IV / Type-III Railway residential quarters or House Rent Allowance
Site Inspection, Night Duty, and Emergency Breakdown allowances for field and workshop engineers
National Pension System (NPS) with 14% Government matching contribution

competition_benchmarks.note: Direct recruitment for Senior Section Engineer (Level-7) was provisionally discontinued in 2018 (RBE No. 166/2018) and formally restored by the Ministry of Railways under Railway Board Circular RBE No. 59/2021 (Letter No. E(NG)II/2018/RR-1/31 dated 06.08.2021). In the previous centralized recruitment drive (CEN 01/2015), over 2,240 SSE vacancies across Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, and S&T disciplines were filled.
